title: Choose FW Lite's design language
question: The roll assigned The Exercise Book. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Exercise Book
options.lineage: the ruled school exercise book that wordlists are first written in, worldwide
options.thesis: Every dictionary starts as words written in a ruled exercise book; FW Lite is that book, kept forever.
materials: a coloured cover for the shell
options.viewport: Sidebar in the project's cover colour; entry list as ruled lines, not cards; the open entry with writing-system codes in the margin left of a red rule and values written on faint baselines.
options.risk: Read timidly it turns into school stationery; it must stay crisp and adult, never doodly or playful.

raised.raise: One ruling system: margin rule, baselines and row dividers are all one device pixel; no shadows carry structure.
State is written in line form as well as colour: dashed pencil rule for unsynced, struck for deleted, solid ink for saved.
A change that arrives by sync stays marked in the margin until you have seen it.
Homograph and sense numbers become one typeset numbering system across list, editor and preview.
Every entry row keeps fixed furniture: headword, gloss and part of speech always in the same places.

options.label: The Thumb Index
options.lineage: printed bilingual dictionaries and their thumb-indexed letter tabs
options.thesis: The app reads like the finished printed dictionary: lexicographic notation, and a thumb index to jump letters.
materials: dictionary notation (bold headword, italic part of speech, numbered senses)
options.viewport: Entry list set as dictionary columns with a thumb-index tab strip down its edge; the open entry shows its printed form first, fields below.
options.risk: The most familiar answer: close to every dictionary website, and one step from the cream-and-serif rut.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain-language labels, and one bright colour that only ever means you can press this.
options.viewport: Same shell on a warm ground; entries as white cards; one green colour reserved for actions only.
options.case: Holds product clarity for community members on phones; loses audience identification because nothing about it says dictionary.
options.risk: Generic: could be any consumer app, and the dictionary disappears.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Two columns round a vermilion rail of keys, apparatus in the margin.
options.viewport: Two twinned columns around a keyed centre rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: scholarly and Western-coded, and the twin columns fight the list-detail layout.
options.kept: Every rule drawn from one ruling system at one device pixel.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Hairline emission lines on charcoal; state carried in line form.
options.viewport: Everything hung off one off-centre rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: a lab instrument, dark and low-contrast for outdoor phones.
options.kept: State written in line form (dashed, struck, solid), not hue alone.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: Rows rerank in place; a change stays lit until noticed.
options.case: Loses both axes: travel ephemera, and entries are not ranked by time.
options.kept: A change that arrives by sync stays marked until seen.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything numbered; colour codes stand in for words.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hurt non-specialists, and black-only fails outdoors.
options.kept: One strict numbering system (homograph and sense numbers).

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: A ranked roster of rounded mascots on pastel.
options.case: Loses both axes: exactly the playful register you ruled out.
options.kept: Fixed furniture: each entry's parts always in the same places.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean neutral productivity app (white, grey, one blue accent), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Today's layout and components, refined to best-in-class polish.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other app by design; still won't feel like a dictionary.
